fieldValues.title: Can an essay container declare its comments and references as children while agents still file into them (srs-web#634)?
fieldValues.decision_question: The owner ruled an essay must export whole from its own container, and that agents never write the essay but may file comments. The engine's write guard protects a container's whole closure, so declaring the comments and references containers as children of the essay container makes agent commenting fail. Which one gives way, or how do both hold?
fieldValues.context: Problem: srs-web#634 asks that the essay container declare its draft, Bin, comments and references containers (as childContainerIds) and its document-state record, so one slice export carries the whole essay. Built and tested against the real engine (branch feat/634-essay-exported-whole): once the comments container is a child of the essay container, an agent session's record_create into it is refused ('container ... is protected'), because the session write guard treats a guarded container's declared children as guarded. The existing test tests/essay-guard.wasm.test.ts fails for exactly this reason. Why it matters: two owner rulings collide. 'An essay can be exported without losing anything' (2026-10-28) needs the children declared; 'agents never write the essay text, they comment' (muDemocracy.org#226) needs agents to write into comments and references. Today the second holds and the first is met only by a separate snapshot bundle that leaves out threads. Options and consequences: see alternatives. Recommendation: A. Action needed: decide. Urgency: blocks srs-web#634 and the muSrs coherence cleanup; no data is at risk meanwhile.
fieldValues.friction: The fix is in the engine's guard semantics (srs-rust), outside the editor builder's mandate (no core change, plan step 5 says file core gaps instead of building them client-side). Doing nothing leaves the export incomplete.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A: the engine guard stops at declared child containers by default, or a guard may list containers it leaves open (srs-rust change, then srs-web#634 builds as planned). B: keep children undeclared on the essay container and keep the snapshot bundle, widened to carry threads and vignettes (no core change; the owner's test 'export from its own container' is not met, the bundle stays). C: declare the children and accept that agents file comments through a different path, for example the essay package gives agents a record type outside the guarded closure (package change, more moving parts). D: do nothing.
fieldValues.key_requirements: One slice export of the essay container carries every record, relation, container and editor state; agents can still file a comment or reference; agents still cannot edit a paragraph body; no client-side reimplementation of engine semantics.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Take A: the write guard protects exactly the containers a session lists, not their declared children (or accepts an explicit open list). File it in srs-rust under semanticops.com#31/#29, then build srs-web#634 as planned; the work-in-progress branch feat/634-essay-exported-whole already contains the editor side.
fieldValues.rationale: One way per goal and capability layering: guard semantics are the engine's. The editor already lists its guarded containers explicitly, so a guard that honours that list is the smallest change and keeps both rulings.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The engine can express per-container guard exceptions some other way, or the owner prefers the bundle (B).
fieldValues.next_steps: 1. Decide A, B, C or D. 2. If A: file the srs-rust issue (guard honours the listed containers only); the builder resumes srs-web#634 once it ships and the pin is bumped. 3. If B: rewrite #634 as widening the bundle.
